coverage: Named roster: FETCHED raw — Wolfe's own accounts of Damon Knight (McCaffery/Science Fiction Studies #46 1988, Dirda/Washington Post 1983, the Locus #500 Wolfe-Gaiman conversation 2002, an undated SF chat transcript, and WolfeWiki's transcription of Contemporary Authors Autobiography Series vol. 9); Hartwell (Wolfe's ranking of his editors in Nova Express 1998, the Urth-of-the-New-Sun paragraph, the Gevers 2002 answer on the Exodus ending, and Hartwell's OWN tribute in the 2012 Fuller Award program PDF); Plant Engineering (Wolfe's 2013 written reply to Nigel Price at Ultan's Library, the magazine's own 2019 obituary, and the Gale and Locus career lines); and C. S. E. Cooney's memoir read in full. NOT FOUND at any route: Knight's Orbit letters themselves (only the Archives West finding aid's description of them) and the text of In Search of Wonder (Wolfe appears only in its 1966 coda, reached through Mark R. Kelly's review; archive.org search-inside hosts do not resolve or time out, and the Google Books API returns nothing). FETCHED BUT WITH NO WOLFE CONTENT: the Locus Hartwell obituary, Patrick Nielsen Hayden's Making Light memorial (which yielded only his judgment of Hartwell), Agranoff's In Search of Wonder review, and Patrick O'Leary's 'If Ever A Wiz There Was' — no Teresa Nielsen Hayden or Tor copyediting anecdote about Wolfe exists at any route tried, which is itself the finding, and a search-engine summary asserting Wolfe's manuscripts were "so clean" was on none of the pages fetched and is not claimed. 27 sources read, 21 substantive: 10 by the named roster, 6 by bibliography chasing (the gwern.net Wolfe document index and the Ultan's Library article list), 5 by lateral search.
